highlights.title: A cleaner task page
highlights.text: A task now opens on the tab that needs you: Plan while it waits for your approval, Result once the agent has built something. The tab shows why with a mark, and the approval card has its own colour only while it waits.

highlights.title: See which agent is on a task
highlights.text: The conversation shows the agent working now, with Resume or Stop beside it. Each message carries its agent's name and mark, and a line marks the moment one agent hands over to another.

highlights.title: A panel that looks like the run workspace
highlights.text: The task's right panel has the run panel's layout: the task as a picker, a thin progress bar, an icon strip down the edge, a collapse button, and quiet Archive and Abandon under the message box.

highlights.title: Tasks on your phone
highlights.text: The bottom bar says Tasks instead of Runs. A task opens as a chat, with the approval card above the message box and the result as a card you open full screen.

fixes: A push made outside the board (by another clone or on GitHub) no longer keeps saying "Not pushed yet"; the board checks quietly in the background.
A task shows your own words as its title instead of "# Request", and the detailed plan is easier to read.
The Plan ready line leaves the conversation once you have answered it.

highlights.title: What's New, right in Settings
highlights.text: After an update, Settings → General → About shows what changed in this release, with a dot on the Settings gear until you have seen it.

highlights.title: See what the agent is doing, live
highlights.text: While Claude Code builds a task, its panel shows the file it is editing or the command it is running right now, with the last few actions below.

highlights.title: Update automatically
highlights.text: A new switch under Settings → General → Updates lets kaizen update itself when nothing is running and no board page is open. Off by default.

highlights.title: A welcome that explains how kaizen works
highlights.text: New users see how a run goes, from ask to review, and the setup no longer ends until a project is added.

highlights.title: Agents offer kaizen's skills
highlights.text: Ask for a video, a deck or a plan in plain chat and the matching skill is offered first.

highlights.title: Permission prompts on the task page
highlights.text: When an agent waits for permission, Allow and Deny are on the task. Kaizen's own file reads no longer ask.

fixes: A task no longer gets stuck after its review; "Looks good" comes back and finishes it.
Explore asks its questions before it starts investigating.
Steam Deck: the app uses software rendering, which stops the GPU crash.
The footer checks your connected phone every 15 seconds.
The last Claude usage reading is kept when its endpoint errors.
